scope: Site copy verified against public v1.35.0: renamable tab titles on /features (added October 16, 2026 before the release went out, as candidates in docs/website-candidate-claims-v1.35.0.json, now retired) and the six interface languages. Also, from October 17, 2026: the newsletter signup card and its Privacy Policy disclosure, and the Blanc Patron page (/patron), whose copy repeats Patron facts already published on the Terms, Privacy and About pages, plus the owner's October 17 priority feature request commitment.

renameTabs.qualification: Tab names (F46): Rename Tab… in the tab context menu and /rename in the ⌘L or Ctrl+L panel set tab.customTitle (renameTab, beginRenameTab in main.js); Reset Tab Title or /rename alone clears it. The name survives navigation, quieting, moving to a new window, reopen-closed (closed-tabs.js), spaces and restart; History and Favorites keep the page title; a private tab’s name is forgotten on quit. Every desktop platform.

interfaceLanguages.qualification: Every translation is status selectable in v1.35.0 (Italian since v1.33.0); machine-made. The interface follows the system language when it matches, or Settings → General → Language, applied after a relaunch. Web pages are not translated.

newsletterPrompt.qualification: Website only, not a browser feature. The signup card (site/src/components/NewsletterPrompt.astro, added after v1.35.0) posts the same {email, website} body to the same /subscribe route as the v1.35.0 footer form, so the double opt-in, retention and honeypot contract the Privacy Policy describes is unchanged. The card itself sends nothing; it keeps one localStorage entry (blanc-newsletter-prompt-v1) with a Not now time or a request time.

privacyRevision.qualification: The Privacy Policy's October 19, 2026 revision only adds the What's New check that ships in v1.39.0 (src/main/whats-new-check.js: one cookie-less HEAD to blanc.day, at most once per launch for up to seven days); its October 17 revision added the newsletter signup card and its browser-local entry. Every other data flow it describes is unchanged.

patronPage.qualification: Patron unlocks no browser features (public since v1.33.0). One checkout link sells the US$4 monthly and US$30 annual plans and the buyer chooses at checkout (docs/polar-setup.md); v1.35.0 Settings → Blanc Patron takes the license key and offers the same link. Cancellation and refunds are under the Terms; the payment provider is named in the Terms and Privacy Policy, and the page names it only by role at the owner's direction (October 17, 2026). The daily subscription check-in data is as the Privacy Policy states. Earlier one-time Supporter licenses activate as lifetime Patron access. Priority feature requests are a service commitment the owner made on October 17, 2026, not browser code: a Patron's emailed request to support@blanc.day from the checkout address is read and answered before general requests; it does not promise that a request ships.

claims.exactWording: Submitting the footer form, or the small signup card that some pages show after you have read for a while, does not immediately subscribe an address. The newsletter Worker temporarily stores the address, request time, and opaque confirmation/unsubscribe material for up to 24 hours and asks Resend to deliver a confirmation email. Resend therefore processes the address for that delivery under its privacy policy. The Worker uses short-lived per-IP rate-limit keys, expiring after about two minutes, but does not attach an IP address to the subscriber record.
claims.subject: Blanc or website

claims.exactWording: The signup card sends nothing on its own. To avoid asking again, it keeps one entry in your browser’s local storage recording when you chose Not now (it stays away for 60 days) or asked to subscribe (it stays away for good). That entry never leaves your browser; clearing site data removes it.
